name: 2979-longprefill-mixtral8x7b-2gpu
hardware: 2x H100 80GB HBM3, two GPUs of one a3 node.
parallelism: TP=2, PP=1, DP=1. Not a free parameter: 93 GB of bf16 weights do not fit one 80 GB card. Widening to TP=4 would be a different setup answering a different question.
architecture: sparse mixture-of-experts decoder (MixtralForCausalLM, 32 layers, 8 experts per layer, top-2 routing per token, hidden 4096, intermediate 14336, 32 query heads / 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, 32768-token window, `sliding_window: null` on this checkpoint's config.json -- full attention, no window). Unquantized bf16: ~93 GB of weights, ~46.7 GB per card at TP=2.
load_profile: constant (open loop), rate 4 req/s, warmup 20%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 600 requests with a 1800 s safety cap -- about 150 s of offered load and 480 scored requests. THE SCORED COUNT IS `max_requests - warmup`, NOT `max_requests - warmup - cooldown`: only the warmup is pinned to `requests` (120 requests, ~30 s at this rate, and it does fire), while the cooldown keeps the default `prefer_duration` and sizes against `safety_seconds` -- `TransientPhaseConfig(percent=0.1).compute_limits(600, 1800)` returns `(180.0, None)`, a 180 s window anchored at t=1620 s that a 150 s run never reaches. It is left declared because an unreached cooldown trims nothing. One consequence matters when reading the output: that unreached boundary becomes `end_time`, so `duration` and `requests_per_second` are pinned by it rather than by the run -- take the true run length from `scheduler_state.start_requests_time` / `end_requests_time`, never from `duration`. Both declared metrics are per-request statistics that a pinned window leaves intact.
workload: synthetic_text, single turn, `request_format: plain`, FIXED length by construction: every request is exactly 1000 prompt tokens and exactly 50 output tokens (min=max on both). No prefix buckets, no length distribution, no shared prefix -- one shape, repeated, so the run measures a single operating point and nothing else. `plain` hands the prompt to the engine as a raw completion string with no chat template and no role wrapper. Per-request sampling is temperature=1.0, top_p=1.0; guidellm's backend forces `ignore_eos` whenever `max_tokens` is set, so every request emits exactly 50 tokens. WIRE LENGTH IS DECLARED LENGTH, and this is measured rather than reasoned. The generator encodes a Faker paragraph, truncates to 1000 ids and decodes with `skip_special_tokens=True`; that encode had itself prepended a BOS, so the decoded string carries 999 content tokens, and vLLM re-adds a BOS when it tokenizes. The two cancel and the engine's own prompt counter reads exactly 1000 -- 200 samples on this checkpoint's tokenizer under guidellm 0.7.3 across two transformers majors, every one of them 1000, none 999 or 1001.
purpose: A sparse mixture-of-experts text completion service generating short 50-token answers from 1000-token prompts at four requests per second across two GPUs.
launch:
# Engine flags for 70f3e8e3a1ed081003c0a2b70de151bb144f98e0 (`git describe --tags`
# v0.3.2-13-g70f3e8e3a1ed), a source checkout named by `configs/env.yaml: venv`.
# Anything not listed here is left at the engine's own default.

# LOCAL PATH: mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1 (revision main) byte for byte -- the same
# weight shards and tokenizer files, linked -- with one key added to config.json:
# `"head_dim": 128` (= hidden_size 4096 / 32 query heads). This engine era's
# ModelConfig.get_head_size() returns hf_config.head_dim whenever the attribute exists, and
# today's transformers sets it to None for this checkpoint, so without the key bring-up dies
# sizing the KV cache: `unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'int' and 'NoneType'`. Build it if
# absent: link every file of the cached snapshot except config.json into the directory, and
# write config.json with head_dim 128 added.
model: ${SYSAGENT_DATA}/models/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1-headdim

# 93 GB of bf16 weights do not fit one 80 GB card, so TP=1 is impossible. TP=4 is a different
# setup answering a different question.
tensor-parallel-size: 2

dtype: bfloat16
max-model-len: 4096
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
